raw_case_text:
A 22-year-old male was evaluated at the ED on March 24, 2014, because of a 3-day history of fever, malaise, myalgia, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache. Physical examination revealed fever, underweight (body mass index = 18.1), and tachycardia. He was given acetaminophen and discharged from the ED with a diagnosis of viral syndrome.
Serum collected on day 2 of illness was negative by PCR and MAT. Convalescent serum collected 18 days after illness onset was positive by MAT with a reciprocal titer of 800 against serogroups Bataviae (serovar Bataviae) and Canicola (serovar Canicola) and was also positive for detection of anti-dengue virus IgM antibodies.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a 3-day history of fever, malaise, myalgia, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed 3 days of acute fever, malaise, myalgia, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache prior to emergency department evaluation on March 24, 2014.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, malaise, myalgia, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile, tachycardic, and underweight with a body mass index of 18.1 kg/m2.
objective.routine_investigations: Acute-phase serum collected on day 2 of illness was negative by PCR and Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT), whereas convalescent serum collected 18 days after symptom onset was positive by MAT with a reciprocal titer of 1:800 against Leptospira serogroups Bataviae (serovar Bataviae) and Canicola (serovar Canicola) and positive for anti-dengue virus IgM antibodies.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Concurrent leptospirosis and dengue virus coinfection, confirmed on day-18 convalescent serum by a Leptospira MAT titer of 1:800 (serogroups Bataviae and Canicola) and positive anti-dengue virus IgM ELISA. Managed as an outpatient with oral acetaminophen.
